content.text:
1. redact: verify JSONL redaction lands, re-encode any line it misses

Hardening statement: redaction output is certified (RedactedBytes), but the certification is currently asserted, not verified. This change backs it with a per-line post-condition and a structural fallback, so the byte-preserving fast path stays byte-preserving and every other line is redacted by construction.

Where: redact/redact.go — applyJSONReplacements (:904), redactJSONLLines (:807), redactSingleJSONValue (:654).

Steps:

1. Refactor the leaf walk to two consumers. collectJSONLReplacements (:991) currently returns (original, redacted) pairs. Extract the walk so it can either collect pairs (fast path, unchanged) or return a redacted copy of the decoded tree, applying the same shouldSkipJSONLField / shouldSkipJSONLObject / credential-context rules. One walk, two outputs, so the skip rules cannot drift apart.
2. Add the post-condition. After applyJSONReplacements returns, and only for lines that had replacements: decode the spliced result and walk its string leaves. If any leaf still equals a replacement's original (honoring the pair's key scoping), the splice did not land. Comparing decoded values against the recorded originals avoids any assumption that the redactor is idempotent.
3. Fall back structurally on a miss. Re-encode the line from the redacted tree (encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false), reattach the line's surrounding whitespace). Formatting fidelity is deliberately sacrificed only for lines the splice could not rewrite. If the marshal itself fails, return an error — JSONLBytes then refuses to certify rather than shipping the line, which is the direction the RedactedBytes contract requires.
4. Apply the same treatment to redactSingleJSONValue, which shares applyJSONReplacements for whole-document content.
5. Tests. The two cases I confirmed on main become regression tests with flipped assertions: a leaf containing raw U+2028 (Go's encoder escapes it even with HTML escaping off, so the search key never matched), and a line using \/. Add: \uXXXX-escaped ASCII, non-ASCII written ensure_ascii-style, a duplicated leaf value, a keyed replacement, and a fast-path test asserting byte-identical output for a line with no encoding variance. My throwaway repro (redact/report_item3_verify_test.go in the scratchpad worktree) can seed these.

Suggested commit message: redact: verify each JSONL splice landed and re-encode lines it cannot rewrite — body: "applyJSONReplacements splices by matching the re-encoded leaf against the raw line. JSON admits more than one encoding of the same string, so a producer's encoding choice could leave a leaf outside the splice's reach with no signal. Redaction now re-checks every spliced line against the collected originals and falls back to a structural re-encode of that line; a line that cannot be rewritten fails the redaction rather than certifying."

---
2. settings: extend the local-provenance gate to agent instruction fields

Hardening statement: the loader already honors exec-bearing settings (openai_privacy_filter.command, external_agents) only from a local file positively verified as the developer's own. Fields that carry verbatim instructions into agents spawned with permission checks disabled belong behind the same gate: investigate.always_prompt and every ReviewConfig.Prompt.

Where: cmd/entire/cli/settings/ — new agent_prompt_trust.go modeled on opf_command_trust.go; call site in loadMergedSettings (settings.go:706); schema fields at settings.go:139 (Review map[string]ReviewConfig), :215, :434 (Agents/Judge), :506 (Investigate.AlwaysPrompt).

Steps:

1. Add enforceAgentPromptTrust(ctx, s, localSettingsPath, localData). For each gated field that is non-empty after merge: keep it only if the local file explicitly sets that key (rawHasKey(raw, "investigate", "always_prompt"); for the review maps, walk rawObject per agent key to the prompt member) and classifyLocalSettingsDeep(ctx, localSettingsPath) == localOwn. Otherwise reset to "" and record the rejected value plus reason, exactly like opf.rejectedCommand. localUnverifiable fails closed here for the same reason it does for the OPF command: these strings get the last word in a prompt that is the stated control for bypassPermissions / --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox spawns (agent/claudecode/spawner.go:25).
2. Cover every ReviewConfig.Prompt reachable in the schema — the top-level review map, the nested Agents map, and Judge. A test that walks the settings schema for ReviewConfig occurrences (like the existing TestAllHookConfigRelPaths_Covers... pattern) keeps a future field from bypassing the gate.
3. Surface the downgrade. Add an accessor mirroring ExternalAgentsRejection(); have investigate and review print a one-line stderr notice naming the dropped field and the file it came from, so a user whose configured preamble stops applying learns why. This mirrors the note already printed when settings fail to reload on --continue (investigate/cmd.go:577).
4. Optional follow-up for shared team preambles: an interactive confirmation that displays the exact project-layer text before honoring it (the shape of confirmUntrustedIssueSeed at investigate/cmd.go:731, with an explicit allow flag). Non-interactive runs keep the drop. Ship the gate first; add this only if teams ask.
5. Judgment call to document in the PR: Skills and Model stay ungated — skills resolve to locally installed content and model is a routing hint — but say so explicitly so the boundary is a decision, not an omission.
6. Tests: mirror the opf_command_trust_test.go matrix — project-set ignored, untracked-local honored, staged/committed local ignored, unverifiable repo keeps the layer but drops the field, and the same set for a review.<agent>.prompt.

Suggested commit message: settings: honor agent instruction fields only from the developer's own local layer — body: "investigate.always_prompt and review prompts are appended verbatim to prompts for agents that run with approvals disabled, so they get the same provenance requirement as the OPF command and external_agents: present in .entire/settings.local.json and that file verified untracked. Rejection downgrades the field and is surfaced on stderr rather than failing the load."

---
3. checkpoint/remote: apply the ownership check to fetch URL resolution

Hardening statement: PushURL only routes to a configured checkpoint_remote after checkpointRemoteIsInherited confirms the setting is ours rather than one that arrived with the clone. FetchURL performs the same routing decision and should apply the same confirmation, so both directions of checkpoint traffic follow one ownership rule.

Where: cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/util.go — fetchURLAuthoritative (:63), checkpointRemoteIsInherited (:405), the doc comment at :184 that documents the asymmetry.

Steps:

1. In fetchURLAuthoritative, after config := s.GetCheckpointRemote() resolves non-nil, run the inheritance check before deriving the checkpoint URL. The push side passes (config, originURL, pushRemoteURLs); the fetch side's identity set is origin plus, when supplied, the LeadReadRemote URL — reuse the existing function with that set rather than writing a second predicate, so the two directions cannot drift.
2. On "inherited", fall through to the no-config path (lead read remote, then origin) and logFallback with the inheritance reason, keeping the existing authoritative=false semantics for the fallback URL so FetchCheckpointRef's absence classification is unaffected.
3. The existing escape hatch already documented at :403 carries over unchanged: a checkpoint repo that is genuinely yours under a different owner is declared in settings.local.json.
4. Cost check: the inherited probe reads remotes and settings; fetch resolution runs inside hooks. If profiling shows it matters, memoize per process the way versionedPaths does (settings/opf_command_trust.go:219) — the answer cannot change within one hook process.
5. Update the docs that describe the asymmetry: the doc comment block at :184 and the README section that justifies the guard on write-side privacy.
6. Tests: the fork-clone topology from checkpointRemoteIsInherited's own doc comment, exercised through FetchURL — committed checkpoint_remote with origin owned by another account resolves to origin, owned topology still resolves to the checkpoint repo, local-layer config still honored.

Suggested commit message: checkpoint/remote: require checkpoint_remote ownership for fetches, matching pushes — body: "PushURL confirms a configured checkpoint_remote is ours before routing writes to it; FetchURL now applies the same check before routing reads, so an inherited setting cannot select the repository that local checkpoint refs are populated from."

---
4. copilotcli: run text generation with the least tool capability the CLI permits

Hardening statement: the Claude text-generation sibling loads no settings precisely so nothing in the input can drive tool execution (agent/claudecode/generate.go:20-24). The Copilot path should state and enforce the same contract instead of --allow-all-tools.

Where: cmd/entire/cli/agent/copilotcli/generate.go:17.

Steps:

1. Verify against the pinned Copilot CLI version what the narrowest non-interactive mode is: first try no approval flag at all (text-only prompts may complete without any tool call); if the CLI requires one, prefer an explicit deny for the shell/write/edit tool classes (--deny-tool) over a blanket allow. Keep --disable-builtin-mcps, the os.TempDir() working directory, and StripGitEnv.
2. Pin the resulting argv in a unit test the way your versioncheck commit pins the auto-updater's command to literals, so a future flag change is a reviewed decision.
3. Add a smoke test that summary generation still completes, since the failure mode of over-restricting is a broken summarizer rather than anything subtle.
4. Port the isolation-contract doc comment from claudecode/generate.go so the reasoning lives at the flag.

Suggested commit message: copilotcli: pin text generation to a minimal tool surface — body: "Summary generation is a text-in text-out call. The subprocess now runs with the narrowest tool policy the CLI supports, matching the isolation contract the Claude generator already documents, and the argv is pinned by test."

---
5. explain: sanitize transcript rendering at the terminal boundary

Hardening statement: checkpoint listings already pass user-influenced text through sanitizeForTerminal before printing. explain --verbose/--full renders transcript content to the same terminal and should go through the same filter.

Where: cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_list.go:150 (existing filter), cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:2151 (appendTranscriptSection), cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go:567 (FormatCondensedTranscript).

Steps:

1. Promote sanitizeForTerminal to a shared home (tuiutil, next to SanitizeDisplayText) and point checkpoint_list.go at it — one implementation, per the exported-SymlinkedEntryError precedent of not letting two producers describe one condition differently.
2. Apply it in explain's rendering of entry.Content, ToolName, and ToolDetail — at the display boundary, not inside FormatCondensedTranscript, since that formatter also builds LLM prompt input where mutation is unwanted.
3. Test: a transcript entry carrying ESC/CSI/OSC sequences renders with them stripped, tabs and newlines preserved.

Suggested commit message: explain: route transcript rendering through the shared terminal sanitizer — body: "checkpoint list already sanitizes prompt text before printing; explain's verbose transcript view now uses the same shared filter, so all terminal rendering of session content passes one sanitization point."

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents. The quality of its work will be significantly higher if run on a platform with subagent support (such as Claude Code or Codex). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Read plan file
2. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
3. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
4. If no concerns: Create TodoWrite and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - Ensures isolated workspace (creates one or verifies existing)
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

146			// In token-based execution path, short-circuit to avoid additional
147			// change in protocol.
148			if originURL != "" {
149				return originURL, false, nil
150			}
151		}
152	
153		if originURL == "" {
154			return "", false, fmt.Errorf("no fetch URL found: %w", originErr)
155		}
156	
157		info, err := ParseURL(originURL)
158		if err != nil {
159			logFallback(ctx, "fetch", originURL, "parse origin remote URL", err)
160			return originURL, false, nil
161		}
162	
163		checkpointURL, err := deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info, config)
164		if err != nil {
165			// Origin's protocol can't be mapped to a checkpoint URL (e.g. file://,
166			// or an entire:// mirror of a different forge than the configured
167			// provider). Honor the configured checkpoint_remote by targeting the
168			// provider's canonical host over HTTPS rather than falling back to origin.
169			if providerURL, ok := resolveProviderCheckpointURL(ctx, config, opt.WorktreeRoot); ok {
170				return providerURL, true, nil
171			}
172			logFallback(ctx, "fetch", originURL, "derive checkpoint remote URL", err)
173			return originURL, false, nil
174		}
175	
176		return checkpointURL, true, nil
177	}

179	// PushURL returns the effective checkpoint push URL for the current repository.
180	// Unlike FetchURL:
181	//   - it derives protocol from the requested push remote, not always origin
182	//   - it skips checkpoint remote use unless origin and EVERY push URL of the
183	//     push remote are owned by the configured checkpoint repo's owner
184	//     (see checkpointRemoteIsInherited); FetchURL applies no ownership check
185	//     at all, so a repo whose writes were diverted still reads from the
186	//     configured checkpoint repo
187	//
188	// If ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN is set, HTTPS is forced so the token can be used
189	// even when the push remote is configured via SSH.
190	//
191	// The boolean return value reports whether a dedicated checkpoint_remote is
192	// configured and should be used for push. When false, the returned URL is the
193	// repository's origin URL as a fallback.
194	func PushURL(ctx context.Context, pushRemoteName string) (string, bool, error) {
195		originURL := ""
196		if resolvedOriginURL, err := GetRemoteURL(ctx, originRemote); err == nil {
197			originURL = resolvedOriginURL
198		}
199	
200		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
201		if err != nil {
202			fallbackURL, fallbackErr := resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx, pushRemoteName, originURL)
203			if fallbackErr == nil {
204				logFallback(ctx, "push", fallbackURL, "load settings", err,
205					slog.String("push_remote", pushRemoteName),
206				)
207				return fallbackURL, false, nil
208			}
209			return "", false, fmt.Errorf("load settings: %w", err)
210		}
211	
212		config := s.GetCheckpointRemote()
213		if config == nil {
214			fallbackURL, fallbackErr := resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx, pushRemoteName, originURL)
215			if fallbackErr != nil {
216				return "", false, fmt.Errorf("no push URL found: %w", fallbackErr)
217			}
218			return fallbackURL, false, nil
219		}
220	
221		// Every push URL, not just the first: git fans out to all of them on the
222		// git-branch backend, so ownership has to hold for the whole set. The first
223		// still drives transport derivation below, matching the single destination
224		// resolveRefsPushDestination sends checkpoint refs to.
225		pushRemoteURLs, err := GetPushURLs(ctx, pushRemoteName)
226		if err != nil {
227			fallbackURL, fallbackErr := resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx, pushRemoteName, originURL)
228			if fallbackErr == nil {
229				logFallback(ctx, "push", fallbackURL, "get push remote URL", err,
230					slog.String("push_remote", pushRemoteName),
231				)
232				return fallbackURL, false, nil
233			}
234			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("no push URL found: %w", err)
235		}
236		pushRemoteURL := pushRemoteURLs[0]
237	
238		// Whether to use the checkpoint remote at all is a question about ownership
239		// ("is this checkpoint_remote mine, or did I inherit it by cloning?"), which
240		// both remotes get a vote on: origin says which project this is, the push
241		// destinations say which repos we are writing to. Any one of them owned by
242		// somebody other than the checkpoint repo's owner means inherited. See
243		// checkpointRemoteIsInherited.
244		if inherited, reason := checkpointRemoteIsInherited(ctx, config, originURL, pushRemoteURLs); inherited {
245			fallbackURL, fallbackErr := resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx, pushRemoteName, originURL)
246			if fallbackErr != nil {
247				return "", false, fmt.Errorf("no push URL found: %w", fallbackErr)
248			}
249			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint-remote: ignoring checkpoint_remote that appears to belong to another owner; pushing checkpoints to the push remote instead",
250				slog.String("checkpoint_repo", config.Repo),
251				slog.String("reason", reason),
252				slog.String("hint", "if this checkpoint repo is yours, configure checkpoint_remote in .entire/settings.local.json"),
253			)
254			return fallbackURL, false, nil
255		}
256	
257		pushInfo, err := ParseURL(pushRemoteURL)
258		if err != nil {
259			if originURL != "" {
260				logFallback(ctx, "push", originURL, "parse push remote URL", err,
261					slog.String("push_remote", pushRemoteName),
262				)
263				return originURL, false, nil
264			}
265			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("no push URL found: %w", err)
266		}
267		withToken := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(CheckpointTokenEnvVar)) != ""
268		if withToken && isDirectGitTransport(pushInfo.Protocol) {
269			// Coerce a direct (ssh/https) remote to HTTPS so the token applies,
270			// keeping the host so enterprise installations stay on their own host.
271			// An entire:// remote carries a cluster host that isn't a usable HTTPS
272			// host, so it's handled separately after the owner check below.
273			//
274			// Keep the port only when the source was already HTTPS. SSH ports
275			// (e.g., :2222) don't map to HTTPS ports on the same host.
276			port := ""
277			if pushInfo.Protocol == ProtocolHTTPS {
278				port = pushInfo.Port
279			}
280			pushInfo = &Info{
281				Protocol: ProtocolHTTPS,
282				Host:     pushInfo.Host,
283				Port:     port,
284				Owner:    pushInfo.Owner,
285				Repo:     pushInfo.Repo,
286			}
287		}
288	
289		if withToken && pushInfo.Protocol == ProtocolEntire {
290			// The checkpoint token is an HTTPS credential for the provider host;
291			// it can't ride through the entire:// helper (which does its own
292			// auth). Route to the provider over HTTPS instead of the mirror.
293			if providerURL, ok := resolveProviderCheckpointURL(ctx, config, ""); ok {
294				return providerURL, true, nil
295			}
296		}
297	
298		pushURL, err := deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(pushInfo, config)
299		if err != nil {
300			// The push remote's protocol can't be mapped to a checkpoint URL
301			// (e.g. file://, or an entire:// mirror of a different forge than the
302			// configured provider). Honor the configured checkpoint_remote by
303			// targeting the provider's canonical host over HTTPS rather than
304			// misrouting checkpoints to the origin remote.
305			if providerURL, ok := resolveProviderCheckpointURL(ctx, config, ""); ok {
306				return providerURL, true, nil
307			}
308			fallbackURL, fallbackErr := resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx, pushRemoteName, originURL)
309			if fallbackErr == nil {
310				logFallback(ctx, "push", fallbackURL, "derive push checkpoint URL", err,
311					slog.String("push_remote", pushRemoteName),
312				)
313				return fallbackURL, false, nil
314			}
315			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("no push URL found: %w", err)
316		}
317	
318		return pushURL, true, nil
319	}

353	// checkpointRemoteIsInherited reports whether the configured checkpoint_remote
354	// looks like it belongs to an upstream project rather than to this developer,
355	// along with a short reason for logging.
356	//
357	// checkpoint_remote is normally committed in .entire/settings.json, so anyone who
358	// forks or clones the project inherits it. Honoring it blindly would push a
359	// contributor's session data into the upstream project's checkpoint repo — which
360	// they typically cannot write to and should not be writing to. This is the check
361	// that guards against that (added in e8b589835 as "fork detection").
362	//
363	// Ownership is decided from local signals only, no network:
364	//
365	//  1. A checkpoint_remote in .entire/settings.local.json is gitignored and
366	//     per-clone, so it cannot have been inherited — it is always ours.
367	//  2. Otherwise EVERY remote that identifies this repo must be owned by the
368	//     checkpoint repo's owner: origin (which project am I working in) and the
369	//     push destination (which repo am I actually writing to). A single
370	//     mismatch means inherited.
371	//
372	// Requiring both is what closes the "cloned the base repo, added my fork"
373	// topology. There are two ways to contribute to someone else's project:
374	//
375	//	fork first, clone the fork  -> origin <fork>/app          -> origin mismatches
376	//	clone the base, add a fork  -> origin <upstream>/app       -> origin MATCHES
377	//
378	// In the second, origin belongs to upstream rather than to us, so an
379	// origin-only check reads an inherited setting as ours and aims a
380	// contributor's transcripts at the upstream project's checkpoint repo. The push
381	// destination is the signal that disagrees: we are writing to <fork>/app.
382	//
383	// The cost, accepted deliberately: a repo of our own with a differently-owned
384	// secondary remote (a backup in another org) no longer routes checkpoints to
385	// our checkpoint repo on pushes to THAT remote — the two topologies are
386	// indistinguishable from local git config alone, since both are
387	// origin=<owner>/app plus a push destination owned by somebody else, and only
388	// the network could say which repo is ours. Pushes to the elected sync remote
389	// (normally origin) are unaffected, and ENT-1451's pre-push gate independently
390	// blocks checkpoint sync on pushes to a non-elected remote, so this costs
391	// nothing that the gate was not already stopping. Erring toward "not ours" is
392	// the safe direction: it never writes session transcripts to a repository we
393	// cannot confirm we own.
394	//
395	// A remote with several push URLs must have EVERY one of them owned by the
396	// checkpoint repo's owner. git fans out to all of them on the git-branch
397	// backend, so checking only the first would let a differently-owned mirror in
398	// second position read as ours.
399	//
400	// An identity whose owner cannot be determined (no remote at all, or a
401	// non-forge URL such as a bare local path) counts as inherited: for a committed
402	// setting we cannot confirm ownership, and falling back preserves the previous
403	// behavior for those repos. settings.local.json is the escape hatch when the
404	// checkpoint repo is genuinely ours but owned by a different account or org.
405	func checkpointRemoteIsInherited(ctx context.Context, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig, originURL string, pushRemoteURLs []string) (bool, string) {
406		checkpointOwner := config.Owner()
407		if checkpointOwner == "" {
408			// No owner to compare (malformed repo field). Matches the predecessor,
409			// which skipped the check rather than blocking on it.
410			return false, ""
411		}
412		if settings.CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly(ctx) {
413			return false, ""
414		}
415	
416		// Both identities when both exist. A repo with no origin has exactly one
417		// identity — its push remote — and must not lose its configured checkpoint
418		// remote just because nothing is named "origin".
419		identities := make([]struct{ url, source string }, 0, 1+len(pushRemoteURLs))
420		if originURL != "" {
421			identities = append(identities, struct{ url, source string }{originURL, "origin"})
422		}
423		for _, pushRemoteURL := range pushRemoteURLs {
424			if pushRemoteURL != "" && pushRemoteURL != originURL {
425				identities = append(identities, struct{ url, source string }{pushRemoteURL, "push remote"})
426			}
427		}
428		if len(identities) == 0 {
429			return true, "no remote to establish ownership"
430		}
431	
432		for _, id := range identities {
433			info, err := ParseURL(id.url)
434			if err != nil || info.Owner == "" {
435				return true, id.source + " URL owner could not be determined"
436			}
437			if !strings.EqualFold(info.Owner, checkpointOwner) {
438				return true, fmt.Sprintf("%s owner %q differs from checkpoint owner %q", id.source, info.Owner, checkpointOwner)
439			}
440		}
441		return false, ""
442	}

462	// isDirectGitTransport reports whether the protocol talks to the git host
463	// directly over ssh/https (where the host is a usable HTTPS host for token
464	// auth), as opposed to a remote helper scheme like entire:// or a local
465	// file://.
466	func isDirectGitTransport(protocol string) bool {
467		return protocol == ProtocolSSH || protocol == ProtocolHTTPS
468	}

470	func deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info *Info, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) (string, error) {
471		switch info.Protocol {
472		case ProtocolSSH:
473			// SCP-style (git@host:repo) doesn't support ports. When a non-default
474			// port is set (e.g., from ssh://git@host:2222/...), use the ssh:// URL form.
475			if info.Port != "" {
476				return fmt.Sprintf("ssh://git@%s/%s.git", info.HostPort(), config.Repo), nil
477			}
478			return fmt.Sprintf("git@%s:%s.git", info.Host, config.Repo), nil
479		case ProtocolHTTPS:
480			return fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/%s.git", info.HostPort(), config.Repo), nil
481		case ProtocolEntire:
482			// entire:// push-through mirrors are cluster-scoped: keep the cluster
483			// host and forge segment, swap in the checkpoint repo. Only derivable
484			// when the forge maps back to the configured provider's host, so a
485			// github checkpoint_remote never routes through another forge's mirror.
486			host, ok := providerHost(config.Provider)
487			if !ok || !strings.EqualFold(info.CanonicalHost(), host) {
488				return "", fmt.Errorf("entire:// remote forge %q does not match checkpoint provider %q", info.Forge, config.Provider)
489			}
490			return fmt.Sprintf("entire://%s/%s/%s", info.HostPort(), info.Forge, config.Repo), nil
491		default:
492			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported protocol %q in remote URL", info.Protocol)
493		}
494	}

496	// resolveProviderCheckpointURL builds the checkpoint URL for the configured
497	// provider, choosing the transport from what's already configured for that
498	// endpoint. It is the fallback used when the push/origin remote's protocol can't
499	// be mapped to a git transport (e.g. entire://, file://): the configured
500	// checkpoint_remote names a concrete provider, so checkpoints go there rather
501	// than being misrouted to the origin remote.
502	//
503	// Transport precedence:
504	//  1. ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN set -> HTTPS on the provider host (the token is
505	//     the credential).
506	//  2. An existing remote already targets the provider host -> reuse its scheme,
507	//     so checkpoints use the same auth the user already has for that endpoint.
508	//  3. Otherwise SSH on the provider host.
509	//
510	// Returns ok=false when no transport can be determined (unknown provider with no
511	// usable signal), in which case the caller falls back to the origin remote.
512	func resolveProviderCheckpointURL(ctx context.Context, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig, dir string) (string, bool) {
513		repo, err := openRepoAt(ctx, dir)
514		if err != nil {
515			repo = nil // Fall back to env/provider-only signals.
516		}
517	
518		info, ok := pickProviderTransport(repo, config)
519		if !ok {
520			return "", false
521		}
522		url, err := deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo(info, config)
523		if err != nil {
524			return "", false
525		}
526		return url, true
527	}

529	// pickProviderTransport returns the protocol/host/port to use when deriving a
530	// checkpoint URL, following the precedence documented on
531	// resolveProviderCheckpointURL.
532	func pickProviderTransport(repo *git.Repository, config *settings.CheckpointRemoteConfig) (*Info, bool) {
533		host, hostOK := providerHost(config.Provider)
534	
535		// 1. Explicit token -> HTTPS on the provider host.
536		if hostOK && strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(CheckpointTokenEnvVar)) != "" {
537			return &Info{Protocol: ProtocolHTTPS, Host: host}, true
538		}
539	
540		// 2. An existing remote already targeting the provider host -> reuse scheme.
541		if hostOK && repo != nil {
542			if info, ok := findRemoteInfoForHost(repo, host); ok {
543				return &Info{Protocol: info.Protocol, Host: info.Host, Port: info.Port}, true
544			}
545		}
546	
547		// 3. Default to SSH on the provider host.
548		if hostOK {
549			return &Info{Protocol: ProtocolSSH, Host: host}, true
550		}
551	
552		return nil, false
553	}

555	// openRepoAt opens the git repository at dir (current directory when dir is
556	// empty). It routes through gitrepo, the single reftable-aware opener, so a
557	// reftable repository is opened via the git-CLI storer rather than rejected by
558	// go-git's extension check. gitrepo.OpenCurrent resolves the worktree root from
559	// the current directory (the walk-up equivalent of the previous DetectDotGit
560	// open) when no explicit root is given.
561	func openRepoAt(ctx context.Context, dir string) (*git.Repository, error) {
562		if dir == "" {
563			repo, err := gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)
564			if err != nil {
565				return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git repository: %w", err)
566			}
567			return repo, nil
568		}
569		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(dir)
570		if err != nil {
571			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git repository: %w", err)
572		}
573		return repo, nil
574	}
575	
576	// findRemoteInfoForHost returns the parsed Info of the first configured git
577	// remote (in deterministic name order) whose host matches host and whose
578	// protocol is a usable git transport (ssh/https). entire:// and other
579	// non-transport remotes are ignored.
580	func findRemoteInfoForHost(repo *git.Repository, host string) (*Info, bool) {
581		cfg, err := repo.Config()
582		if err != nil {
583			return nil, false
584		}
585		names := make([]string, 0, len(cfg.Remotes))
586		for name := range cfg.Remotes {
587			names = append(names, name)
588		}
589		sort.Strings(names)
590		for _, name := range names {
591			for _, rawURL := range cfg.Remotes[name].URLs {
592				info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(rawURL)
593				if err != nil {
594					continue
595				}
596				if strings.EqualFold(info.Host, host) && isDirectGitTransport(info.Protocol) {
597					return info, true
598				}
599			}
600		}
601		return nil, false
602	}

604	func deriveTokenOriginURL(originURL string) (string, bool) {
605		info, err := gitremote.ParseURL(originURL)
606		if err != nil {
607			return "", false
608		}
609		if info.Host == "" || info.Owner == "" || info.Repo == "" {
610			return "", false
611		}
612		// Keep the port only when the source was already HTTPS. SSH ports
613		// (e.g., :2222) don't map to HTTPS ports on the same host.
614		hostPort := info.Host
615		if info.Protocol == ProtocolHTTPS {
616			hostPort = info.HostPort()
617		}
618		return fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/%s/%s.git", hostPort, info.Owner, info.Repo), true
619	}

621	func providerHost(provider string) (string, bool) {
622		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(provider)) {
623		case "github":
624			return "github.com", true
625		case "gitlab":
626			return "gitlab.com", true
627		default:
628			return "", false
629		}
630	}

643	func logFallback(ctx context.Context, operation, fallbackURL, reason string, err error, attrs ...any) {
644		logAttrs := []any{
645			slog.String("operation", operation),
646			slog.String("fallback_url", RedactURL(fallbackURL)),
647			slog.String("reason", reason),
648			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
649		}
650		logAttrs = append(logAttrs, attrs...)
651		logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint remote URL resolution fell back to alternate remote URL", logAttrs...)
652	}
653	
654	func resolvePushFallbackURL(ctx context.Context, pushRemoteName, originURL string) (string, error) {
655		if originURL != "" {
656			if strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(CheckpointTokenEnvVar)) != "" {
657				if tokenURL, ok := deriveTokenOriginURL(originURL); ok {
658					return tokenURL, nil
659				}
660			}
661			return originURL, nil
662		}
663		if pushRemoteName == "" {
664			return "", fmt.Errorf("no push remote specified and remote %q not found", originRemote)
665		}
666		if pushRemoteName == originRemote {
667			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote %q not found", originRemote)
668		}
669		pushURL, err := GetRemoteURL(ctx, pushRemoteName)
670		if err != nil {
671			return "", err
672		}
673		if strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(CheckpointTokenEnvVar)) != "" {
674			if tokenURL, ok := deriveTokenOriginURL(pushURL); ok {
675				return tokenURL, nil
676			}
677		}
678		return pushURL, nil
679	}

50	// WithWorktreeRoot returns a context that makes settings.Load resolve project
51	// and clone-local settings relative to worktreeRoot instead of the process cwd.
52	func WithWorktreeRoot(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string) context.Context {
53		if worktreeRoot == "" {
54			return ctx
55		}
56		return context.WithValue(ctx, worktreeRootContextKey{}, filepath.Clean(worktreeRoot))
57	}

59	// WorktreeRoot returns the explicit worktree root carried by ctx. Consumers
60	// that combine settings resolution with repo-local git commands use this to
61	// keep both operations scoped to the same repository.
62	func WorktreeRoot(ctx context.Context) (string, bool) {
63		return worktreeRootFromContext(ctx)
64	}

66	func worktreeRootFromContext(ctx context.Context) (string, bool) {
67		root, ok := ctx.Value(worktreeRootContextKey{}).(string)
68		return root, ok && root != ""

245	// SummaryGenerationSettings configures provider selection for on-demand
246	// checkpoint summaries generated by explain --generate.

248		// Provider is the selected summary provider agent name
249		// (for example "claude-code", "codex", "gemini", or "pi").
250		Provider string `json:"provider,omitempty"`

256	// Validate returns an error if the settings combination is semantically invalid.
257	// A model without a provider is meaningless: the model hint needs a provider to
258	// route to. The load path calls Validate() after merging, catching hand-edited
259	// files that land in this state.
260	func (s *SummaryGenerationSettings) Validate() error {
261		if s == nil {
262			return nil
263		}
264		if s.Model != "" && s.Provider == "" {
265			return fmt.Errorf("summary_generation.model %q set without summary_generation.provider", s.Model)
266		}
267		return nil
268	}
269	
270	// SetProvider updates the provider and optionally the model, clearing any stale
271	// model from the previous provider when switching without a replacement.
272	// An empty newProvider preserves the current provider; an empty newModel
273	// preserves the current model unless the provider is changing, in which case
274	// the old model is cleared to avoid passing (say) a Claude model to Codex.
275	func (s *SummaryGenerationSettings) SetProvider(newProvider, newModel string) {
276		if s == nil {
277			return
278		}
279		if newProvider != "" && s.Provider != "" && s.Provider != newProvider && newModel == "" {
280			s.Model = ""
281		}
282		if newProvider != "" {
283			s.Provider = newProvider
284		}
285		if newModel != "" {
286			s.Model = newModel
287		}
288	}

343	// the runtime currently supports, and DisallowUnknownFields will reject any
344	// future user who tries to set it. Adding the field again should land in
345	// lockstep with the runtime enforcement.
346	type OPFSettings struct {
347		Enabled    bool            `json:"enabled,omitempty"`

350		// Command is executed, so Load() honors it only when it is
351		// developer-owned — set in an untracked .entire/settings.local.json — and
352		// resets it to "" otherwise. See enforceOPFCommandTrust. Readers that
353		// obtain settings by any route other than Load() (LoadFromFile,

361		// the user had unset it. See enforceOPFCommandTrust.

411	// ReviewProfileConfig is a named review setup. The profile-level Task is the
412	// canonical task every reviewer agent is asked to run; per-agent ReviewConfig
413	// entries adapt that task to agent-specific mechanics such as slash commands
414	// or additional instructions. Judge names the single agent that consolidates
415	// the reviewers' reports into the final verdict in a closing round.
416	//
417	// Example:
418	//
419	//	"review_profiles": {
420	//	  "security": {
421	//	    "task": "Review this change for auth, injection, secrets, and privilege-boundary bugs.",
422	//	    "agents": {
423	//	      "claude-sonnet": {"agent": "claude-code", "model": "sonnet", "skills": ["/security-review"]},
424	//	      "codex": {"model": "gpt-5-codex", "skills": ["/review"], "prompt": "Focus on security."}
425	//	    },
426	//	    "judge": {"agent": "claude-code", "model": "opus"}
427	//	  }
428	//	}

430	// ReviewProfileConfig is intentionally small: the review package owns built-in
431	// default task text for conventional profile names like "general".
432	type ReviewProfileConfig struct {
433		Task   string                  `json:"task,omitempty"`
434		Agents map[string]ReviewConfig `json:"agents,omitempty"`
435		// Judge is the single agent (plus optional model) that consolidates the
436		// reviewers' reports into the final verdict. It is optional: a
437		// one-reviewer profile needs no judge (the lone report is the result),
438		// and a multi-reviewer profile with no judge set falls back to an
439		// auto-selected reviewer that can write a verdict.
440		Judge *ReviewConfig `json:"judge,omitempty"`
441		// Output selects where the final review verdict is delivered: "local"
442		// (printed and saved to the local review manifest — the default) or
443		// "trail" (additionally posted to the branch's trail as a finding via
444		// the data API). Empty means local.
445		Output string `json:"output,omitempty"`
446	}
447	
448	// IsZero reports whether the profile is effectively unset.
449	func (c ReviewProfileConfig) IsZero() bool {
450		return c.Task == "" && len(c.Agents) == 0 && (c.Judge == nil || c.Judge.IsZero())
451	}

453	// ReviewConfig holds one worker's configuration within a review profile.
454	// The profile's agents map is keyed by worker id. For simple configs the worker
455	// id is also the agent registry name (for example "claude-code"). To run the
456	// same agent more than once with different models, use stable worker ids and set
457	// Agent to the underlying registry name.
458	//
459	// Skills are agent-specific invocations passed before the task. Prompt is
460	// additional agent-specific instruction appended after the profile task; it is
461	// no longer a verbatim replacement for the whole review prompt.
462	type ReviewConfig struct {
463		// Agent is the underlying agent registry key for this worker. Empty means
464		// the profile map key is the agent name. Set this when the map key is an
465		// alias such as "claude-sonnet" or "claude-opus".
466		Agent string `json:"agent,omitempty"`
467	
468		// Model is an optional model hint passed to the agent CLI for this worker.
469		// Empty means use the agent's own default.
470		Model string `json:"model,omitempty"`
471	
472		// Skills is the list of slash-prefixed skill invocations configured
473		// for this agent. May be empty for prompt/model-driven workers (e.g. Pi),
474		// in which case the profile task plus Prompt drive the review.
475		Skills []string `json:"skills,omitempty"`
476	
477		// Prompt, when non-empty, carries saved agent-specific instructions. It is
478		// appended after the profile task (and after any Skills); it is not a
479		// verbatim replacement for the whole review prompt.
480		Prompt string `json:"prompt,omitempty"`
481	}

483	// IsZero reports whether the config is effectively unset.
484	func (c ReviewConfig) IsZero() bool {

490	// all configured agents, so the schema is a flat agent list with global
491	// loop knobs rather than per-agent skill lists.
492	type InvestigateConfig struct {
493		// Agents is the ordered list of agent names to round-robin during the loop.

496		// MaxTurns is the per-agent turn budget. Defaults to 2 when zero

498		MaxTurns int `json:"max_turns,omitempty"`

501		// Zero means "all agents must approve" (matches marvin's default).
502		Quorum int `json:"quorum,omitempty"`
503	
504		// AlwaysPrompt is appended to every turn's composed prompt, parallel
505		// to ReviewConfig.Prompt.
506		AlwaysPrompt string `json:"always_prompt,omitempty"`
507	}

509	// IsZero reports whether the config is effectively unset.
510	func (c *InvestigateConfig) IsZero() bool {
511		if c == nil {
512			return true
513		}
514		return len(c.Agents) == 0 && c.MaxTurns == 0 && c.Quorum == 0 && c.AlwaysPrompt == ""
515	}

517	// LocalLayerRejection reports why .entire/settings.local.json was ignored, or
518	// "" when it was applied (or absent). A tracked local file is not local: it
519	// arrives by cloning, so honoring it would let one developer's overrides —
520	// including ones that pick binaries to execute — apply to everyone.
521	func (s *EntireSettings) LocalLayerRejection() string {

529	// untrusted, and whether a rejection happened. Callers that would otherwise

585	// Load loads the Entire settings from .entire/settings.json, then applies
586	// clone-local preferences from the git common dir, then applies any overrides
587	// from .entire/settings.local.json if it exists.
588	// Returns default settings if no settings or preferences file exists.
589	// Works correctly from any subdirectory within the repository.
590	func Load(ctx context.Context) (*EntireSettings, error) {
591		if worktreeRoot, ok := worktreeRootFromContext(ctx); ok {
592			return loadForWorktreeRoot(ctx, worktreeRoot)
593		}
594	
595		settingsFileAbs, localSettingsFileAbs, err := settingsAbsPaths(ctx)
596		if err != nil {
597			return nil, err
598		}
599		preferencesFileAbs := ""
600		if path, prefErr := ClonePreferencesPath(ctx); prefErr == nil {
601			preferencesFileAbs = path
602		} else {
603			// Log at Debug rather than silently dropping the preferences layer.
604			// "Not in a git repo" is a legitimate case (some commands run outside
605			// a repo), but a git PATH issue or .git/ permission failure is worth
606			// finding via `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` when users report "my picker
607			// choices vanished".
608			logging.Debug(ctx, "clone preferences path unresolved; skipping preferences layer",
609				slog.String("error", prefErr.Error()))
610		}
611	
612		return loadMergedSettings(ctx, settingsFileAbs, preferencesFileAbs, localSettingsFileAbs)
613	}

615	// settingsAbsPaths resolves the base and local settings file paths against the
616	// repository anchor. Resolution failures are returned rather than converted to
617	// cwd-relative paths: doing the latter can select a different .entire from a
618	// subdirectory precisely when Git could not establish which repository owns it.
619	func settingsAbsPaths(ctx context.Context) (base, local string, err error) {
620		// entiredir.PathTo, not paths.AbsPath: both files live under .entire, and
621		// entiredir owns the one anchor for that directory. AbsPath's failure mode
622		// here was a relative path that then resolved against the process's own
623		// directory, which is the thing the anchor exists to prevent.
624		base, err = entiredir.PathTo(ctx, EntireSettingsFile)
625		if err != nil {
626			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("resolve project settings path: %w", err)
627		}
628		local, err = entiredir.PathTo(ctx, EntireSettingsLocalFile)
629		if err != nil {
630			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("resolve local settings path: %w", err)
631		}
632		return base, local, nil
633	}

645			preferencesFileAbs = path
646		} else {
647			logging.Debug(ctx, "clone preferences path unresolved; skipping preferences layer",

653	func clonePreferencesPathForWorktreeRoot(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string) (string, error) {
654		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", worktreeRoot, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
655		output, err := cmd.Output()
656		if err != nil {
657			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve git common dir: %w", err)
658		}
659	
660		commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
661		if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
662			commonDir = filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, commonDir)
663		}
664		return filepath.Join(filepath.Clean(commonDir), ClonePreferencesFile), nil
665	}

667	func loadMergedSettings(ctx context.Context, settingsFileAbs, preferencesFileAbs, localSettingsFileAbs string) (*EntireSettings, error) {
668		// Load base settings
669		settings, err := loadFromFile(settingsFileAbs)
670		if err != nil {
671			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading settings file: %w", err)
672		}
673	
674		if preferencesFileAbs != "" {
675			preferences, err := loadClonePreferencesFromFile(preferencesFileAbs)
676			if err != nil {
677				return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading clone preferences file: %w", err)
678			}
679			applyClonePreferences(settings, preferences)
680		}
681	
682		// Apply local overrides if they exist — but only from a file that is
683		// genuinely local. See localLayerTrackedReason.
684		localData, err := readConfined(localSettingsFileAbs)
685		if err != nil {
686			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
687				return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading local settings file: %w", err)
688			}
689			// Local file doesn't exist, continue without overrides
690		} else if classifyLocalSettings(ctx, localSettingsFileAbs) == localTracked {
691			// Dropped only on PROOF that the file is tracked. Discarding every
692			// local setting because a repository could not be read would be a
693			// worse failure than the one being guarded against — the exec-bearing
694			// OPF command applies the stricter policy for itself.
695			settings.localLayerRejection = localLayerTrackedReason
696			localData = nil
697		} else if err := mergeJSON(settings, localData); err != nil {
698			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merging local settings: %w", err)
699		}
700	
701		// openai_privacy_filter.command is executed, so it is honored only from a
702		// local file positively verified as this developer's own. external_agents
703		// grants execution of every entire-agent-* binary on $PATH, so it gets the
704		// same gate.
705		enforceOPFCommandTrust(ctx, settings, localSettingsFileAbs, localData)
706		enforceExternalAgentsTrust(ctx, settings, localSettingsFileAbs, localData)
707	
708		// Re-validate after merge. Individual files are validated by loadFromFile,
709		// but mergeJSON patches fields independently and can produce combinations
710		// (e.g. model without provider when the local override sets only a model
711		// on top of a base with no provider) that neither file alone contained.
712		if err := settings.SummaryGeneration.Validate(); err != nil {
713			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merged settings invalid: %w", err)
714		}
715	
716		if err := validateScannerSettings(settings); err != nil {
717			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merged settings invalid: %w", err)
718		}
719	
720		return settings, nil
721	}

886	// readConfined reads filePath through an os.Root, refusing outright to read it
887	// if it is a symbolic link.
888	//
889	// The root confines the open to its directory, so the read cannot be redirected
890	// outside it by a swapped or symlinked path between resolution and open
891	// (TOCTOU) — unlike a bare os.ReadFile of an absolute path. Callers must
892	// classify "missing" with errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) rather than
893	// os.IsNotExist, since the returned errors are wrapped.
894	//
895	// WHICH root is chosen by where the path is, not by whether an open succeeded:
896	// a path under .entire is read through the shared root every other .entire
897	// consumer uses, and a permission failure there must surface rather than
898	// silently retry through a second root. The other branch is not a weaker path
899	// but a different directory — this same function also reads clone preferences
900	// out of the git common dir, which .entire has no claim on.
901	//
902	// Confinement alone is NOT the invariant, which is why readConfinedIn also
903	// Lstats. Entire's config files are never read through a link, wherever it
904	// points, and os.Root leaves two gaps against that:
905	//
906	//   - A RELATIVE link whose target stays inside the directory is followed
907	//     without complaint. `.entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json` is the
908	//     case that matters: that file names the command Entire executes at
909	//     pre-push, so following it hands the far end a say in what runs.
910	//   - A DANGLING link surfaces as ENOENT, which every caller here reads as
911	//     "absent" and answers with default settings. A planted
912	//     `.entire/settings.json -> missing.json` therefore made Entire silently
913	//     ignore the project's settings rather than fail.
914	//
915	// An absolute target, and a relative one that escapes, were already refused —
916	// but as "path escapes from parent", which describes neither the cause nor the
917	// fix. All four now give the same verdict and the same remedy.
918	//
919	// This overlaps paths.ValidateEntireDirAt, which rejects a symlinked entry in
920	// `.entire` before a command runs at all. The duplication is deliberate: that
921	// guard hangs off the root pre-run and cli.LoadEntireSettings, while eighteen
922	// files call settings.Load directly — the strategy hook paths among them — and
923	// this is the read those callers have in common.
924	func readConfined(filePath string) ([]byte, error) {
925		// Branch on WHERE the path is, not on whether the open succeeded: a
926		// permission failure inside .entire must surface, not silently retry
927		// through a second root.
928		if _, _, underEntire := entiredir.Split(filePath); !underEntire {
929			return readConfinedOutsideEntire(filePath)
930		}
931	
932		// A relative path is resolved against the process's directory, which is what
933		// "relative" means and what LoadFromFile's callers pass deliberately. The
934		// anchor rule entiredir enforces is about code that DERIVES a .entire path
935		// (see settingsAbsPaths, which now goes through entiredir.PathTo); it is not
936		// a reason to refuse a path a caller handed us.
937		filePath, err := filepath.Abs(filePath)
938		if err != nil {
939			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve settings path: %w", err)
940		}
941	
942		root, name, err := entiredir.OpenPathForRead(filePath)
943		if err != nil {
944			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open settings dir: %w", err)
945		}
946		return readConfinedIn(root, name, filePath)
947	}
948	
949	// readConfinedOutsideEntire reads the clone-preferences file, which lives in the
950	// git common dir rather than under .entire, through that directory's shared
951	// root.
952	//
953	// The fallback anchors on the file's own parent, and that is the one shape this
954	// codebase otherwise refuses — see the "an os.Root's base must be a trusted
955	// path" rule. It is allowed here for the same reason tokenstore's is: the paths
956	// that reach it are ones the CALLER named (the explicit-path settings tests, and
957	// LoadFromFile's callers), so their parent directory is the caller's choice too
958	// and there is no separate trusted base to prefer. It never applies to a path
959	// Entire derived — those are placed under a common dir by clonePreferencesRoot
960	// above, or under .entire by readConfined's other branch.
961	func readConfinedOutsideEntire(filePath string) ([]byte, error) {
962		if root, name, err := clonePreferencesRoot(filePath); err == nil {
963			return readConfinedIn(root, name, filePath)
964		}
965	
966		root, err := os.OpenRoot(filepath.Dir(filePath))
967		if err != nil {
968			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open settings dir: %w", err)
969		}
970		defer root.Close()
971	
972		return readConfinedIn(root, filepath.Base(filePath), filePath)
973	}
974	
975	// readConfinedIn is the one read every readConfined branch performs: refuse a
976	// symlink, open, re-validate against the race, then read.
977	//
978	// It exists so the refusal cannot be true of one branch and not another. It was
979	// briefly true of only one: the .entire branch read straight through
980	// osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently — precisely the
981	// `.entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json` case the check exists for.
982	//
983	// filePath is carried alongside name only for the error text: name is relative
984	// to a root the caller cannot see, and the user needs the path they can act on.
985	func readConfinedIn(root *os.Root, name, filePath string) ([]byte, error) {
986		data, err := osroot.ReadFileNoFollow(root, name)
987		if err != nil {
988			if errors.Is(err, osroot.ErrSymlinkedPath) {
989				//nolint:wrapcheck // sentinel surfaces verbatim for the caller's errors.Is; callers add the reading-context prefix
990				return nil, paths.SymlinkedEntryError(filePath)
991			}
992			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read settings file %s: %w", filePath, err)
993		}
994		return data, nil
995	}
996	
997	// writeConfinedAtomic is readConfined's write half: an atomic write through the
998	// shared .entire root, or through the git common dir's root for the clone
999	// preferences file. It creates the parent directory, which for a .entire path
1000	// means the root itself.
1001	//
1002	// The non-.entire branch used to be a plain os.MkdirAll plus an unrooted atomic
1003	// write, which made the two halves asymmetric for no reason: readConfined
1004	// already resolved that same file through clonePreferencesRoot. A write is the
1005	// half that matters more, so it gets the same root.
1006	func writeConfinedAtomic(filePath string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error {
1007		// Same branch-on-location rule as readConfined.
1008		if _, _, underEntire := entiredir.Split(filePath); !underEntire {
1009			return writeClonePreferencesAtomic(filePath, data, perm)
1010		}
1011	
1012		// Same relative-path handling as readConfined.
1013		filePath, err := filepath.Abs(filePath)
1014		if err != nil {
1015			return fmt.Errorf("resolve settings path: %w", err)
1016		}
1017	
1018		root, name, err := entiredir.OpenPath(filePath)
1019		if err != nil {
1020			return fmt.Errorf("creating settings directory: %w", err)
1021		}
1022		if dir := path.Dir(name); dir != "." {
1023			if err := osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink(root, dir, 0o750); err != nil {
1024				return fmt.Errorf("creating settings directory: %w", err)
1025			}
1026		}
1027		return jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn(root, name, data, perm) //nolint:wrapcheck // caller names the file being written
1028	}
1029	
1030	// writeClonePreferencesAtomic writes a file that lives in the git common dir
1031	// rather than under .entire, through that directory's root.
1032	//
1033	// A path clonePreferencesRoot cannot place inside a common dir keeps the plain
1034	// unrooted write: the callers that reach it name a file directly (explicit-path
1035	// tests, and `entire disable` in a directory with no repository), and there is
1036	// no boundary to enforce for a path the caller chose itself.
1037	func writeClonePreferencesAtomic(filePath string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error {
1038		root, name, err := clonePreferencesRoot(filePath)
1039		if err != nil {

1090	func loadClonePreferencesFromFile(filePath string) (*ClonePreferences, error) {
1091		prefs := &ClonePreferences{}

1101		// Lenient decoding here (vs. strict via DisallowUnknownFields in
1102		// loadFromFile for EntireSettings). Two reasons clone preferences need

1133	// mergeReviewProfiles overlays src review profiles onto base by name, returning
1134	// a new map. A profile from a higher-precedence layer (src) overrides the
1135	// same-named one from a lower layer (base), but profiles unique to each layer
1136	// are all preserved. This lets a team keep shared profiles in
1137	// .entire/settings.json while individuals add or override profiles in
1138	// clone-local preferences or .entire/settings.local.json, without one layer

1143	// result is always a fresh, non-nil map (empty when both inputs are empty), so
1144	// callers never receive nil from a non-nil input.
1145	func mergeReviewProfiles(base, src map[string]ReviewProfileConfig) map[string]ReviewProfileConfig {
1146		out := make(map[string]ReviewProfileConfig, len(base)+len(src))
1147		for name, cfg := range base {
1148			out[name] = cfg
1149		}
1150		for name, cfg := range src {

1156	func modifyClonePreferencesFile(filePath string, fn func(*ClonePreferences) error) error {

1186	// file's name inside it.
1187	//

1189	// filePath, not by walking up a fixed number of parents. Both produce the same

1191	// filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(abs)) form silently anchored one directory too high

1196	// constant is a shape assertion instead: a path that is not
1197	// <git-common-dir>/entire/preferences.json is refused rather than opened
1198	// somewhere else.
1199	func clonePreferencesRoot(filePath string) (*os.Root, string, error) {
1200		abs, err := filepath.Abs(filePath)
1201		if err != nil {
1202			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("resolve preferences path: %w", err)
1203		}
1204		suffix := string(filepath.Separator) + filepath.FromSlash(ClonePreferencesFile)

1206		if !ok || commonDir == "" {
1207			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not a %s inside a git common dir", filePath, ClonePreferencesFile)
1208		}

1210		if err != nil {
1211			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("open git common dir: %w", err)
1212		}
1213		return root, name, nil
1214	}

1216	func applyClonePreferences(settings *EntireSettings, prefs *ClonePreferences) {
1217		if prefs == nil {
1218			return
1219		}
1220		if prefs.ReviewProfiles != nil {
1221			settings.ReviewProfiles = mergeReviewProfiles(settings.ReviewProfiles, prefs.ReviewProfiles)

1223		if prefs.ReviewDefaultProfile != "" {

1225		}
1226		if prefs.Review != nil {

1228		}

1231		}

1234	// mergeJSON merges JSON data into existing settings.
1235	// Most fields only apply non-zero values from JSON. The review map is replaced
1236	// whenever the key is present, so override files can clear or fully replace
1237	// project-level review configuration.
1238	func mergeJSON(settings *EntireSettings, data []byte) error {
1239		// Validate that there are no unknown keys using strict decoding.
1240		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))

1243		if err := dec.Decode(&temp); err != nil {
1244			return fmt.Errorf("parsing JSON: %w", err)
1245		}
1246	
1247		// Parse into a map to check which fields are present.
1248		var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
1249		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
1250			return fmt.Errorf("parsing JSON: %w", err)
1251		}
1252	
1253		if err := mergeScalarFields(settings, raw); err != nil {

1255		}

1257			return err
1258		}
1259		if err := mergeSummaryGeneration(settings, raw); err != nil {
1260			return err
1261		}
1262		if err := mergeCommitLinking(settings, raw); err != nil {
1263			return err
1264		}
1265		if profilesRaw, ok := raw["review_profiles"]; ok {
1266			var profiles map[string]ReviewProfileConfig
1267			if err := json.Unmarshal(profilesRaw, &profiles); err != nil {
1268				return fmt.Errorf("parsing review_profiles field: %w", err)
1269			}
1270			// Merge per-profile so a local override file adds to / overrides shared
1271			// profiles by name rather than replacing the whole set.
1272			settings.ReviewProfiles = mergeReviewProfiles(settings.ReviewProfiles, profiles)
1273		}
1274		if reviewRaw, ok := raw["review"]; ok {
1275			var review map[string]ReviewConfig
1276			if err := json.Unmarshal(reviewRaw, &review); err != nil {
1277				return fmt.Errorf("parsing review field: %w", err)
1278			}

1280		}

1283		if redactionRaw, ok := raw["redaction"]; ok {

1286			}

19	// localLayerTrackedReason explains why a tracked .entire/settings.local.json
20	// is ignored.
21	//
22	// The whole point of the local layer is that it is per-clone and per-developer:
23	// it is gitignored, it is where `entire enable --local` writes, and other code
24	// treats "present in the local file" as proof the developer chose it
25	// personally. A tracked local file breaks that premise — .gitignore does not
26	// apply to a path that is already tracked, so `git add -f
27	// .entire/settings.local.json` commits it and a fresh clone materializes it
28	// with whatever the committer put there. It then silently overrides project
29	// settings for everyone who clones, which is both a correctness surprise and,
30	// for settings naming a binary to execute, a way to run code on other people's
31	// machines through an ordinary pull request.
32	//
33	// Rejection ignores the layer rather than failing the load. Erroring would let
34	// one committed file brick every Entire command in the repo — including
35	// `status` and `doctor`, the tools needed to diagnose it.
36	const localLayerTrackedReason = "it is tracked in git, so it is not local to this clone — it arrives with the repository and overrides project settings for everyone"
37	
38	// enforceOPFCommandTrust drops redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command unless
39	// it came from a local file positively verified as this developer's own.
40	//
41	// The command becomes argv[0] of an exec in the pre-push OPF rewrite (see
42	// redact.ConfigurePrivacyFilter -> newShellOut), so whoever controls the string
43	// controls what Entire runs on the developer's machine. .entire/settings.json
44	// is version-controlled, so honoring it from there would let an ordinary pull
45	// request carry a command pointing at a payload committed alongside it — and a
46	// JSON settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push
47	// prompt is no defense: it never names the command, prompt_default "always"
48	// skips it, and non-TTY pushes auto-run.
49	//
50	// localData is the raw local-file bytes, nil when the file is absent or its
51	// layer was dropped as tracked. When the command does come from there, this
52	// re-verifies with the deep (index AND HEAD) check and requires localOwn:
53	// unlike the layer as a whole, an unverifiable repository fails CLOSED here,
54	// because the cost of being wrong is executing an attacker's binary rather
55	// than losing a preference.
56	//
57	// Rejection is a downgrade, never an error: Command resets to "" and
58	// ConfigurePrivacyFilter falls back to resolving "opf" on $PATH, which Go's
59	// exec.ErrDot protects against "." entries. If that binary is missing, the
60	// pre-push rewrite fails closed rather than pushing content the user believed
61	// OPF had scanned.
62	func enforceOPFCommandTrust(ctx context.Context, s *EntireSettings, localSettingsPath string, localData []byte) {
63		if s == nil || s.Redaction == nil || s.Redaction.OpenAIPrivacyFilter == nil {
64			return
65		}
66		opf := s.Redaction.OpenAIPrivacyFilter
67		if opf.Command == "" {
68			return
69		}
70	
71		var reason string
72		switch {
73		case !localSetsOPFCommand(localData):
74			reason = "it did not come from .entire/settings.local.json"
75		case classifyLocalSettingsDeep(ctx, localSettingsPath) != localOwn:
76			reason = "the local settings file could not be verified as untracked"
77		default:
78			return
79		}
80	
81		// Record rather than log, for two reasons. A log line in
82		// .entire/logs/entire.log is not a signal the user will see, and the
83		// consumer can put this on stderr where it belongs. And the loader is
84		// reached while the cli package resolves the log level, so keeping it
85		// log-free keeps it off any future re-entrancy path into the logger
86		// (Init no longer calls out under its lock, but the loader should not
87		// depend on that).
88		opf.rejectedCommand = opf.Command
89		opf.rejectionReason = reason
90		opf.Command = ""

93	// localSetsOPFCommand reports whether the local override file explicitly sets
94	// redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command.

97	// and the local file may set the same string, and comparing effective values
98	// after the merge would misattribute that to the project layer. A malformed
99	// local file yields false, which is the safe direction — the merge itself
100	// fails separately with a parse error.
101	func localSetsOPFCommand(data []byte) bool {
102		var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
103		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
104			return false
105		}
106		return rawHasKey(raw, "redaction", "openai_privacy_filter", "command")
107	}

109	// rawHasKey reports whether a nested key is present in a decoded JSON object,
110	// walking objects along the way. A missing or non-object link yields false.
111	//
112	// Presence is the question, not value: two layers may set the same string, so
113	// comparing effective values after a merge would misattribute provenance.
114	//
115	// The first key is a separate parameter rather than part of the variadic so

118	// predicate that gates a security boundary. This shape makes the compiler
119	// reject it instead of relying on every caller to pass enough arguments.
120	func rawHasKey(parent map[string]json.RawMessage, first string, rest ...string) bool {
121		key := first
122		for _, next := range rest {
123			parent = rawObject(parent, key)
124			key = next
125		}
126		_, ok := parent[key]
127		return ok
128	}

131	// is absent or does not hold an object. Indexing the nil result is safe, so
132	// lookups can be chained without intermediate checks.
133	func rawObject(parent map[string]json.RawMessage, key string) map[string]json.RawMessage {
134		v, ok := parent[key]
135		if !ok {
136			return nil
137		}
138		var out map[string]json.RawMessage

145	// localTrust is the loader's verdict on .entire/settings.local.json.

150	// required, because losing every local setting over an unreadable repository

155	const (
156		localUnverifiable localTrust = iota // repository could not be read
157		localTracked                        // proven present in the index (or HEAD, for a deep check)

159	)

161	// classifyLocalSettings checks the git index only.
162	//
163	// The index is what a delivered attack shows up in: a pull request that
164	// commits .entire/settings.local.json puts it in the index of every clone that
165	// checks the branch out. HEAD is deliberately NOT consulted here. The only
166	// state the index misses is "committed, then git rm --cached", and checkout
167	// does not produce a file that is absent from the index — so that state is one
168	// the local developer created, not one that arrived with the repository.
169	//
170	// Skipping HEAD is what keeps this affordable for the broad population. On a
171	// packed repository the HEAD commit+tree lookup costs more than the index
172	// parse, and on a reftable repository it re-enters the git CLI (gitrepo routes
173	// reference reads through a subprocess there), which is ~150x the cost of the
174	// index check.
175	func classifyLocalSettings(ctx context.Context, path string) localTrust {
176		return classify(ctx, path, false)
177	}

179	// classifyLocalSettingsDeep also checks HEAD, catching content that is
180	// committed but no longer staged. Reserved for the OPF command, where being
181	// wrong means executing someone else's binary and the extra cost is paid only
182	// by the few users who set that field locally.
183	func classifyLocalSettingsDeep(ctx context.Context, path string) localTrust {
184		return classify(ctx, path, true)

187	func classify(ctx context.Context, path string, deep bool) localTrust {
188		switch versioned, err := localSettingsIsVersioned(ctx, path, deep); {

190			return localUnverifiable
191		case versioned:
192			return localTracked
193		default:

202		path string

212	// may be transient.

214	// Process-scoped, which is right for hooks but stale for a long-lived `entire

238	func localSettingsIsVersioned(ctx context.Context, path string, deep bool) (bool, error) {
239		key := probeKey{path: path, deep: deep}

241		versionedPathsMu.Lock()

249		if err != nil {

259	// probeLocalSettingsIsVersioned answers through go-git rather than the git CLI.
260	// Beyond avoiding a subprocess, this removes a dependency on `git` being on
261	// $PATH for ordinary repositories — the population running GUI git clients,
262	// whose hooks do not inherit a shell profile, is precisely the one that needs
263	// an explicit OPF command and would otherwise fail verification and lose it.

269	// no git call is needed to resolve either. That coupling is load-bearing: if

271	// the grandparent would name the wrong directory. It holds today because
272	// readConfined can only have succeeded on the relative form when the working
273	// directory IS the worktree root.
274	func probeLocalSettingsIsVersioned(ctx context.Context, path string, deep bool) (bool, error) {
275		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
276			return false, fmt.Errorf("verify %s: %w", EntireSettingsLocalFile, err)

279		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(path)))

282			// cloning when there is nothing to clone, so this is a definitive
283			// "not versioned", not a verification failure. Treating it as a
284			// failure would drop the local layer for every non-repo invocation.
285			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {

289		}

291	
292		// Index. Paths are stored slash-separated, which EntireSettingsLocalFile
293		// already is, on every platform.
294		idx, err := repo.Storer.Index()
295		if err != nil {
296			return false, fmt.Errorf("read index: %w", err)
297		}
298		for _, entry := range idx.Entries {
299			if pathsEqualFold(entry.Name, EntireSettingsLocalFile) {
300				return true, nil
301			}
302		}
303		if !deep {
304			return false, nil
305		}
306	
307		// HEAD. An unborn HEAD cannot contain the file, so that is a definitive
308		// negative rather than a verification failure.
309		head, err := repo.Head()
310		if err != nil {
311			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
312				return false, nil
313			}
314			return false, fmt.Errorf("resolve HEAD: %w", err)
315		}
316		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
317		if err != nil {
318			return false, fmt.Errorf("read HEAD commit: %w", err)
319		}
320		tree, err := commit.Tree()
321		if err != nil {
322			return false, fmt.Errorf("read HEAD tree: %w", err)
323		}
324		return treeHasPathFold(tree, strings.Split(EntireSettingsLocalFile, "/"))
325	}
326	
327	// pathsEqualFold reports whether two repo-relative git paths can name the same
328	// working-tree file once the filesystem has had its say.
329	//
330	// The comparison must NOT be exact, because git records the committed name
331	// while readConfined opens the canonical one, and several filesystems map the
332	// two together:
333	//
334	//   - Case. On a case-insensitive volume (the macOS and Windows default) a pull
335	//     request can commit `.entire/Settings.Local.json`; checkout materializes a
336	//     file that readConfined opens through the canonical name.
337	//   - Trailing dots and spaces. Win32 strips them, so a committed
338	//     `.entire/settings.local.json.` also lands on disk under the canonical
339	//     name. This is the class core.protectNTFS defends, but that setting only
340	//     guards .git-family names, not ours.
341	//
342	// Either way the file would be read as settings while an exact lookup judged
343	// it untracked — precisely the bypass this gate exists to prevent, and for the
344	// trailing-dot case reachable through an ordinary pull request, since it
345	// defeats the index check rather than only the HEAD one.
346	//
347	// Normalizing unconditionally rather than probing the platform is deliberate:
348	// no variant of this filename is ever legitimate content, so treating one as
349	// tracked on Linux too costs at most an ignored local layer plus a warning,
350	// and it keeps the security-relevant path free of a capability check that
351	// could itself be wrong.
352	//
353	// Residual limits worth knowing. This covers Unicode simple case folding and
354	// the Win32 trailing-character rule, not every equivalence a filesystem might
355	// apply (NFC/NFD, for instance); the filename is pure ASCII, so those are not
356	// the realistic vectors. NTFS alternate data streams are a read-side suffix
357	// rather than a committable name, and 8.3 short names are generated aliases
358	// for long names rather than the reverse, so neither is a route in.
359	func pathsEqualFold(a, b string) bool {
360		return strings.EqualFold(normalizePathForFilesystemCompare(a), normalizePathForFilesystemCompare(b))
361	}
362	
363	// normalizePathForFilesystemCompare drops the trailing dots and spaces Win32
364	// strips, per path component. A component that is nothing but those characters
365	// (".", "..") is left alone: emptying it would change the path's meaning.
366	func normalizePathForFilesystemCompare(path string) string {
367		parts := strings.Split(path, "/")
368		for i, part := range parts {
369			if trimmed := strings.TrimRight(part, ". "); trimmed != "" {
370				parts[i] = trimmed
371			}
372		}
373		return strings.Join(parts, "/")
374	}
375	
376	// treeHasPathFold reports whether any fold-matching chain of tree entries
377	// spells parts. object.Tree.FindEntry matches exactly, so it cannot be used.
378	//
379	// It must try EVERY fold-matching entry at each level, not just the first.
380	// Git objects are case-sensitive, so one tree can legitimately hold both
381	// `.Entire` and `.entire`, and git sorts uppercase first — so a decoy that
382	// sorts earlier (a blob by that name, or a directory missing the child) would
383	// otherwise mask the real sibling and produce a false negative. That is the
384	// "any variant is tracked" semantics the index scan already has; the two sides
385	// of this predicate must not disagree.
386	func treeHasPathFold(tree *object.Tree, parts []string) (bool, error) {
387		if len(parts) == 0 {
388			return false, nil
389		}
390		part, rest := parts[0], parts[1:]
391	
392		for i := range tree.Entries {
393			entry := &tree.Entries[i]
394			if !pathsEqualFold(entry.Name, part) {
395				continue
396			}
397			if len(rest) == 0 {
398				return true, nil
399			}
400			sub, err := tree.Tree(entry.Name)
401			if err != nil {
402				if errors.Is(err, object.ErrDirectoryNotFound) {
403					continue // a blob where a directory was expected: try siblings
404				}
405				return false, fmt.Errorf("read %s in HEAD: %w", entry.Name, err)
406			}
407			found, err := treeHasPathFold(sub, rest)
408			if err != nil {
409				return false, err
410			}
411			if found {
412				return true, nil
413			}
414		}
415		return false, nil
416	}
